papers.label: E-0 reference-psyche transfer (ours)
papers.f3_note: WORST overstatement ratio in the entire frame, ours. Mem0's is 200.0.
papers.f4_note: H1 reports z = -16.03 and p_one_sided = 1.0 over 3141 items. Clustering by the 4 repositories deflates |z| by sqrt(DEFF): to 2.53 at rho=0.05, 1.04 at rho=0.3, and 0.57 at rho=1. Our own inference is computed over items, not repositories. We commit the exact error we document.
papers.f5_note: The comparator was a retry-count controller, a different system. No condition populated the psyche state and blocked its influence.
papers.f8_quote: preregistration = docs/research/experiments/e0-preregistration.md; H1 criterion 'delta>=0.02 and p<0.01', H2 criterion '>=0.54', H3 criterion '>0.52' all fixed in advance
papers.f8_note: Possibly the only paper in the frame coding preregistered on F8. This is the one dimension where we outperform the audited literature.
papers.f9_note: 37 instances excluded as error_eval_or_timeout out of 6018 replayed; the exclusion is recorded rather than silent.
papers.claimed_effect: H1 delta = -0.367 AUC (0.339 vs 0.705); verdict FAIL on all three hypotheses
papers.paired: paired; same evaluation instances under both conditions
flags: The clustering error worked AGAINST us. E-0's conclusion was negative - the psyche lost to a retry-count baseline - so item-level inference inflated confidence in a FAILURE. At proper clustering we could not have concluded that either. We over-claimed a null.
This is reported because the same statistical error inflates negative claims as readily as positive ones, and an audit that applied its critique only to favourable results would be dishonest.
Determinism was verified: all traces byte-identical across two replays. That is a real strength and is reported alongside the failure.
